questions.explanation: The crude rate has a moving denominator and a numerator whose age profile is heavily weighted to the oldest bands, so it falls if the number of old people falls even when nothing has improved at any particular age. Life expectancy is assembled from age-specific rates of dying and so is far less sensitive to the shape of the pyramid, which is why the two can move apart for a decade.
